boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus spaces for studying, gathering, reflection, and student-led activity, with access details where Stanford publishes them.

cards.title: Cecil H. Green Library
cards.subtitle: 557 Escondido Mall
cards.notes: Start here when your group needs tables or you need a quieter reading break; check library access and hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Stanford’s largest library combines humanities and social-sciences collections with group and quiet study options.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Libraries identifies Green as its largest library and says it offers group study spaces and quiet places to read, work, and recharge.
cards.source_title: Cecil H. Green Library | University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Some spaces and after-hours access require a Stanford ID; consult current library hours.

cards.title: Media & Microtext Center
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Green East
cards.notes: Bring a partner for a flexible work session, then use the on-site media stations or browse the film and game collections.
cards.short_summary: A Green Library space with tables for individual or group study alongside extensive media equipment and collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Libraries says the Media & Microtext Center has ample tables for individual or group study and media viewing stations and gaming consoles.
cards.source_title: Media & Microtext Center at Cecil H. Green Library | University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Located on the lower level of Green East; noise levels may vary with use.

cards.entity_name: Robin Li and Melissa Ma Science Library
cards.title: Robin Li and Melissa Ma Science Library
cards.subtitle: 376 Lomita Drive
cards.notes: Use the reading and study areas for a focused session near science collections; ask staff when research questions stall you.
cards.short_summary: A science-library setting with quiet study and reading areas surrounded by research collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Libraries describes the Science Library as offering quiet study and reading spaces amid collections for science and engineering fields.
cards.source_title: Robin Li and Melissa Ma Science Library | University Libraries
cards.access_notes: Check Stanford Libraries for current building access and hours.

cards.entity_name: Branner Earth Sciences Library Group Study Cubicles
cards.title: Branner Group Study Cubicles
cards.subtitle: Branner Earth Sciences Library & Map Collections
cards.notes: Meet here for a small working session when a whiteboard and monitor would help; the listing says reservations are not required.
cards.short_summary: Named small-group study cubicles equipped for conversation, visual work, and natural-light study.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Libraries lists Branner’s Group Study Cubicles for two to four people with a monitor, whiteboard, natural light, and conversation space.
cards.access_notes: The library listing says reservation is not required; confirm current access before visiting.

cards.title: Tresidder Memorial Union
cards.subtitle: 459 Lagunita Drive
cards.notes: Use the patio seating or meet inside before a campus program; student groups can consult Meeting Services for reservable spaces.
cards.short_summary: A student-union hub for dining, meetings, programs, and everyday campus gatherings.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Campus Spaces describes Tresidder as a hub for community activities with dining, patio seating, and nearby event space.
cards.access_notes: Reservable rooms and events are coordinated through Student Affairs Meeting Services.

cards.title: Old Union
cards.subtitle: 520 Lasuen Mall
cards.notes: Stop by for student-organization connections, a meeting, or a recharge between classes; use the accessible side paths if needed.
cards.short_summary: Stanford’s student-union complex includes meeting rooms, student-affairs offices, cultural centers, and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Campus Spaces calls Old Union a central hub for student activities and lists meeting rooms, student-affairs offices, and cultural centers.
cards.access_notes: The building has power-door and elevator access; individual services and rooms may have separate access rules.

cards.title: White Plaza
cards.subtitle: White Memorial Plaza
cards.notes: Walk through to see campus notices and scheduled activity, or have your recognized student group review the tabling and event rules.
cards.short_summary: A designated campus forum for student programs, speeches, information tables, fairs, banners, and posters.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford designates White Plaza for student and university programs, speeches, events, information tables, fairs, banners, and posters.
cards.access_notes: Events are for recognized student organizations and university units and must follow Stanford’s space policies.

cards.title: Meyer Green
cards.subtitle: Central campus lawn
cards.notes: Use the lawn as a central meet-up point or attend a registered low-impact gathering; keep paths clear and check event requirements first.
cards.short_summary: A central outdoor lawn Stanford identifies for low-impact gatherings and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford Campus Spaces describes Meyer Green as a spacious central location for low-impact events and gatherings.
cards.source_title: Campus Spaces | Student Affairs Meeting Services
cards.access_notes: Student groups and Stanford affiliates can reserve the lawn or stage; larger events may need additional coordination.

cards.title: Windhover Contemplative Center
cards.subtitle: 370 Santa Teresa Street
cards.notes: Plan a device-free reflection break here, and bring your Stanford ID; leave food, drinks, cameras, and laptops outside.
cards.short_summary: A campus contemplative center created for quiet reflection and personal renewal.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford’s Office for Religious & Spiritual Life describes Windhover as a spiritual refuge for quiet reflection and personal renewal.
cards.source_title: Visit Windhover Contemplative Center | Office for Religious & Spiritual Life
cards.access_notes: Valid Stanford ID is required to enter; guests are not allowed, and the building closes for university holidays and winter closure.

cards.title: Windhover Labyrinth
cards.subtitle: Adjacent to Windhover, 370 Santa Teresa Street
cards.notes: Take a slow outdoor loop beside Windhover when you want a reset between commitments; keep the space contemplative for others.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor labyrinth beside the contemplative center that Stanford identifies as open for public use.
cards.evidence_claim: Stanford’s Office for Religious & Spiritual Life states that the outdoor labyrinth adjacent to Windhover is for public use.
cards.source_title: Windhover Contemplative Center | Office for Religious & Spiritual Life
cards.access_notes: The labyrinth is outdoors adjacent to Windhover; follow posted campus guidance.
